Understanding Web Accessibility

March 15, 2024 By Sarah Johnson Accessibility

Why Accessibility Matters

Web accessibility ensures that websites and web applications are usable by people with disabilities. This includes individuals who use screen readers, keyboard navigation, or other assistive technologies.

The Four Principles of WCAG

The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) are organized around four principles:

  1. Perceivable — Information must be presentable to users in ways they can perceive.
  2. Operable — User interface components must be operable.
  3. Understandable — Information and operation must be understandable.
  4. Robust — Content must be robust enough for a variety of user agents.

Common Accessibility Issues

Here are some of the most frequently encountered accessibility problems:

  • Missing alternative text on images
  • Poor color contrast ratios
  • Missing form labels
  • Inaccessible keyboard navigation
  • Missing document language

Testing Your Website

Automated tools like axe-core can catch many accessibility issues, but manual testing with assistive technologies is also essential for comprehensive coverage.

"The power of the Web is in its universality. Access by everyone regardless of disability is an essential aspect." — Tim Berners-Lee
